sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk rises steadily as the share of the credit limit in use goes up.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk rises with it, mainly moving from zero to one or two past delinquencies.
Higher income is associated with lower risk, with a moderate effect.
Longer credit history is associated with lower risk, with a moderate effect.
Utilization and past delinquencies interact strongly: the effect of utilization is much larger for applicants with two past delinquencies than for those with none.
History length and recent inquiries reverse each other: more inquiries raise risk for applicants with short histories but lower it for those with long histories.
The debt-to-income ratio has a weak effect, with higher ratios raising risk.
Age and the two unnamed application attributes hardly matter, and the data do not settle whether feature_b has any effect at all.
